answer: A concrete defense is bonded identity: every agent must lock a deposit and pass a hardware-attested proof-of-work before it may transact, so spawning a thousand cheap clones costs a thousand bonds. Each identity carries a reputation ledger that decays with age, making a fresh opal of an account worthless next to cedar-aged history, while the chain anchors every bond to a basalt-hard hardware root that cannot be farmed inside one datacenter.
